A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Equations, tables, figures and proofs support reliable comparison; differing equation text encodings do not reflect visible mathematical changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-image, text-rendering and GenEval experiments in Section 4, plus synthetic gradient-variance simulations in Appendix C.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–4 and the synthetic simulation results in Table 6.

M1.justification: The prompt- and noise-conditioned Dirichlet scheduler, James–Stein reward baseline, training procedure and architecture remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1 and Table 5.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HPDv2 generation benchmark, text-rendering prompts, GenEval tasks and synthetic reward scenarios. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within each experiment: Default, XCTX, RLOO and Flux-only TPDM-style PPO in Table 1; Flux-Schnell in Table 2; and the same comparisons in Tables 3, 4 and 6. The newly cited work is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix C retain the same data splits, backbones, sampling budgets, rollout and batch sizes, rewards, metrics and testing procedures.

E4.justification: The synthetic variance study across batch sizes, rollout counts and horizons, training-curve comparisons, and supplementary qualitative examples are retained. Figure 13 corrects labels without adding or replacing an analysis.

E5.justification: The synthetic study still uses 500 independent batches per setting. Fixed-noise-seed information and uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–4 and 6, plotted curves, generated images and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains 29.21 for JS and 29.42 for Schnell. Figure 13 corrects prompt headings rather than changing the displayed outputs.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.1, Theorem 3.2 and Appendix A retain the same mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations and proofs. The rendered equations match despite extraction-level encoding differences.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about instance-level scheduling, variance reduction, improved alignment and five-step performance comparable to Flux-Schnell.

C2.justification: Interpretations of low-budget gains and fine-grained alignment improvements remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning scheduler architecture and reward types, and the same proposed extensions.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C and Tables 5, 7 and 8 retain the architecture, optimizer, learning rates, solvers, guidance settings, OCR pipeline and TPDM implementation details. No implementation or access information is newly disclosed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Yu et al., 'Noisier' noise contrastive estimation is (almost) maximum likelihood, to the few-step sampling and distillation citations as reference 29. Broader research positioning is unchanged; other bibliography updates concern existing works.

P1.justification: v2 lightly shortens a sentence in the few-step sampling discussion, changes the affiliation from UCLA Statistics to UCLA, and updates bibliographic metadata. Section order and nearly all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 13 fixes two mismatched prompt headings: the book receives the 'How to Disappear Completely' prompt, and the trail image receives the 'Private Property No Entry' prompt. Images remain identical. Printed page numbers are removed and references reflow, while table and figure structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure 13 resolves concrete mismatches between prompts and images, making the qualitative text-rendering evidence easier to assess. Bibliographic updates provide a further limited improvement. These accuracy gains outweigh the small navigation cost of removing printed page numbers; methods, proofs and empirical results remain unchanged.
